meaning: The number 403 appears in the Bible's genealogy from Shem to Abraham as the lifespan of the patriarchs Arpachshad and Shelah.
description: The number 403 appears twice in the Bible, both times in the genealogy of Genesis 11. Arpachshad lived 403 years after he fathered Shelah (Gen 11:13), and Shelah lived 403 years after he fathered Eber (Gen 11:15). It is remarkable that the same number is used for both patriarchs, which underscores the structured and symmetrical arrangement of the genealogy from Shem to Abraham. This genealogy serves as a bridge between primeval history and the patriarchal narratives, and the long lifespans reflect a gradual decline in life expectancy from the generations before the flood. Although 403 has not attained prominent independent symbolic status in Jewish or Christian tradition, its occurrence in this theologically important family tree is meaningful as part of biblical chronology.

versions.meaning: The number 403 has no well-established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
versions.description: 403 is not a number highlighted specifically in the Bible or in traditional Jewish numerology (gematria) with an acknowledged symbolic role. It can be decomposed into Hebrew letter values (for example, tav = 400 and gimel = 3), but this does not yield a combination with known symbolic tradition attached to it. In gematria, many words may have the numerical value of 403, but none of these have gained prominent symbolic status in the broader Jewish or Christian tradition.
versions.reason: [major] Description ignores that the number 403 actually occurs explicitly in the Bible – in Genesis 11:13 and 11:15, where both Arpachshad and Shelah lived 403 years after having their sons. This is a concrete biblical occurrence that should be mentioned.; [minor] The Meaning field could be more precise. Although the number does not have an established symbolic meaning, it should mention the biblical context (years of life in the genealogy from Shem to Abraham).; [minor] It is worth noting the letter combination tav (400) + gimel (3) in a footnote with possible symbolic interpretation, since tav is often linked to completion/sign and gimel to goodness/exaltation in rabbinic tradition.

footnotes.text: In Hebrew, 403 can be written with the letters tav (ת = 400) and gimel (ג = 3). Tav is the last letter of the Hebrew alphabet and is associated with completion and signs (cf. Ezek 9:4), while gimel is traditionally linked to gemilut chasadim (acts of kindness). However, this combination has not received any established symbolic interpretation.

The genealogy in Genesis 11:10–26 shows a systematic decline in lifespan from Shem (600 years total) down to Terah (205 years). The fact that both Arpachshad and Shelah share the lifespan of 403 may point to a deliberate literary structuring of the text.
